plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Reduce exposure to AI/Software (METU, MSFU, PLTU) and Semiconductors (MUU) to zero.
Trim Income (QQQI) to 20% to build cash buffer.
Hold remaining Broad Index (SPY, QQQ) and Tech (CRWD, SNOW, SMCI) positions.

conservative.read: This mode aims for low, steady gains with minimal drawdowns. Expect slower growth, prioritizing capital safety over aggressive returns. Risk is significantly reduced, but upside potential is also capped.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to a small percentage.
Reduce concentration in AI/Software (METU, MSFU, PLTU) and Semiconductors (MUU).
Add a new quality tech name (AMZN) to the portfolio.
Maintain a balanced mix of broad index, income, and quality tech.
This plan seeks growth while managing risk by reducing leverage and concentration.
A moderate cash buffer will be held.
balanced.read: This mode targets moderate growth with a focus on risk management. It balances potential upside with downside protection. Expect growth that is more consistent but less explosive than aggressive modes. Drawdowns are expected to be manageable.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and concentrate in AI/Software (METU, MSFU, PLTU) and Semiconductors (MUU).
Add a high-conviction tech name (NVDA) to the portfolio.
This plan leans into high-growth sectors and uses leverage to amplify potential returns.
A smaller cash buffer will be maintained to maximize invested capital.
Strict stop-loss discipline is crucial due to increased leverage and concentration.
Expect higher volatility and potential for larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This mode aims for aggressive growth by concentrating in high-potential sectors and utilizing leverage. It carries significantly higher risk, including the potential for substantial drawdowns and amplified losses due to leverage and daily rebalancing of ETFs. Upside potential is maximized, but so is the risk of rapid, large losses.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta tech/semiconductor names (CRWD, SMH).
Eliminate exposure to broad growth indices (QQQ, SPY).
Increase allocation to Income (QQQI) to maximize monthly distributions.
This plan prioritizes generating steady income over capital appreciation.
It aims for low volatility and predictable cash flow.
While income is prioritized, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
income.read: This mode focuses on generating consistent monthly income with minimal volatility. Growth potential is sacrificed for stability and yield. Expect lower overall returns compared to growth-oriented modes, but with a more predictable income stream. Drawdowns are expected to be very limited.
